feat: Improve agent edit UI (#348)

* ui improvements

* Improve agent edit UI for profiles and agents

* fix ci

* convert machines to machine binding id

* review fixes, adapt to document based yaml

* Refresh agent on config save conflict so discard loads the latest config

A 409 left the cached agent (and its current_config_id) stale, so
discarding remounted the editor with the same old source and expected id,
conflicting again on retry. Invalidate the agent query on 409 (awaited
before the mutation settles) and make discard re-snapshot from the live
query instead of falling back to the stale snapshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Skip already-listed machines when granting from a source row

Granting from a row's combobox could duplicate machine_name entries and
reassign a selected row while keeping its cwd/env overlays. Drop names
already in the list, fill the current row only when it's empty, and
append the rest as fresh rows. Also apply prettier formatting CI flagged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reconcile agent config editor with main's React Doctor refactor

The rebase onto main replayed this branch's editor rewrite over the
React Doctor restructuring (#308), so re-apply main's changes the replay
dropped and bring the editor suite in line with the new CI gate:

- Restore main's machines.ts (atomic connectByoMachine) and DataTable
  column API in AgentProfilesSection, re-applying this branch's edits.
- Adapt the machine source comboboxes to the new resource-combobox
  value contract via lightweight option objects.
- Fix React Doctor findings: refs instead of render state for
  handler-only values, drop compiler-redundant memoization, set-based
  lookups, and resolve the skills cache during render instead of an
  effect. Ignore the parent-callback rules for the editor files, whose
  children intentionally report yaml/dirty/availability upward.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Parse the config source once per editor via a serialization session

deserializeBasicConfig and applyBasicConfig each took the raw source, so
every builder change re-parsed the baseline and re-extracted it into a
second draft. createBasicConfigSession(source) parses and extracts once
for the editor's lifetime and returns { initialDraft, apply }; apply
clones the pristine document per call so reverting a field restores the
entry's original formatting. The form takes the session instead of
initialConfig + baselineSource.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Replace hand-rolled config extraction with a zod schema

extractBasicConfig walked the parsed document with manual typeof checks,
per-entry key allowlists, and generic list/map plumbing. A zod schema
now declares the builder-representable subset directly: strictObject is
the key allowlist, looseObject is the tolerated-extras top level, and
what remains is the typed mapping into draft rows. On the apply side,
tools and MCP entries compare by wire form, removing the parallel
comparable shapes; only machine sources keep a distinct comparison form,
since pool-resolution backfill changes their wire output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Consolidate the config editors and slim the mode machine

The agent panel editor and profile editor duplicated the mode machine
wiring, blocked/dirty/saveBlocked derivation, and the tabs/builder/YAML
layout. useAgentConfigEditor now owns that state and
AgentConfigEditorFields the shared markup; the editors keep only their
form, messages, and footer.

The mode reducer tracks just the hand-edited YAML (null while mirroring
the builder) instead of holding both buffers; builder YAML lives with
the component that produces it. wireConfig is gone — the no-document
fallback applies onto an empty Document through the same path as every
other serialization. The form's duplicate BasicConfigDraft type is
replaced by BasicConfig.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Strip comments and give the builder form a document-facing hook

Remove the explanatory comments this PR added across the frontend and
Go changes, keeping only functional directives. useAgentBuilderForm now
owns the builder draft: it seeds from the session's document, exposes
form values and named setters, and reports serialized YAML plus the
blocked flag; AgentConfigBasicForm is rendering only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fold agentConfigBasic into useAgentBuilderForm

The draft types, empty draft, and completeness check belong to the form.
isBasicConfigComplete becomes per-section validators (draftValid,
machineSourceValid, mcpServerValid, mcpServerNamesUnique) private to the
hook; other modules import the draft types from useAgentBuilderForm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move the document session and apply into useAgentBuilderForm

The hook is the only thing that applies drafts to the document, so
agentConfigBasicYaml.ts folds into it: session creation, the
diff-and-rewrite apply, and the wire serializers now live with the form
that uses them. The two test files and their fixtures merge into
useAgentBuilderForm.test.ts. agentConfigBasicExtract.ts stays separate
as the schema-validated read side (folding it in would break the
500-line lint limit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Adopt builder-representable YAML edits when switching back to the builder

Switching from the YAML tab to the builder previously always demanded
discarding hand edits. Now the typed YAML runs through
createBasicConfigSession: when it is builder-representable it becomes
the new session baseline and the form reseeds from it, so the edits
carry over; the confirm-and-discard dialog remains only for YAML the
builder cannot represent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Derive builder YAML from the form instead of mirroring it upward

The editor held builderYaml state fed by an onYamlChange callback
because the draft lived inside the form component. useAgentBuilderForm
no longer takes a callback: the editor hook owns the form, and yaml and
blocked are derived from the draft (session.apply(draft)). That deletes
the mirror state, the callback effect, and the formGeneration remount on
YAML adoption, which now just resets the draft. AgentConfigBasicForm
takes the form object and stays render-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix YAML adoption: collapse the fork with an explicit action

Adopting builder-representable YAML edits never worked: switchMode
collapsed the fork by dispatching editor-yaml-changed with the forked
text itself, which the reducer's no-op guard swallowed, so switch-mode
still saw a fork and raised the discard dialog for every edit. A
dedicated adopt-yaml-edits action enters the builder and clears the
fork; reducer tests pin the transitions. The dialog copy now says it
only appears for YAML the builder can't represent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prune library-behavior and duplicate tests

Drop the form tests that only exercised the yaml/zod libraries
(formatting-variant parsing, explicit empty parameters, irregular
instruction indentation) and merge the discard reducer test into the
confirm-dialog transition it belongs to; adopt keeps its own regression
test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gofmt agent_config_changes_store.go

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Regenerate sqlc code after SQL comment removal

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Integrate main's agent templates with the builder-form create page

Rebase reconciliation: main added an onboarding template flow built on
agentConfigBasicSerialization, which this branch had replaced with the
useAgentBuilderForm session API. Rewrite CreateAgentFormView on the new
API (template menu, ?template= prefill, message placeholder preserved),
re-point agentTemplates at the builder module, and delete the retired
serialization module. Carry main's GB memory rename through the builder
form, extract, and machine sources field. Regenerate the TS SDK from the
merged spec.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Serialize an untouched builder form to an empty YAML document

With no baseline config, applyToDocument wrote empty-string scalars into
a fresh document, so the YAML tab on the create page opened with an
instruction/model skeleton instead of an empty editor and typed YAML
merged into it invalidly. Compare scalars against an empty baseline so
only filled fields are written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): canonicalize email identity keys (#466)

Email identity keys were lower(trim(email)), so the composed, decomposed
and Punycode spellings of an internationalized domain were three
different identities: logins and invitations missed each other and a
second account could be verified for the same mailbox.

Derive the key in one place (internal/emailaddr): the domain becomes its
lowercase A-label via UTS #46 non-transitional processing with hostname
length rules, the comparison form RFC 9598 §5.5 prescribes; the local
part is lowercased and otherwise left alone, since RFC 9598 §5.7 forbids
transforming it and merging two spellings a mail server might treat as
different mailboxes would attach an OIDC login to the wrong account.
CreateUserEmail derives the key itself instead of trusting callers.
Lookups stay single-key and no queries change. Every pure-ASCII key is a
fixed point of the new rule (property-tested), so existing rows keep
their keys and no data migration is needed.

emailaddr.Equal replaces the EqualFold comparison of OIDC id-token and
userinfo emails. The password policy receives the address rather than
the key and rejects a password containing either spelling.

Supersedes #409.

fix: make agent event streams resilient (#421)

* fix: make agent event streams resilient

* chore: prune redundant comments

* fix(api): reconcile missed SSE event wakeups

* docs: focus SSE guide on client behavior

* refactor(sdk): own the SSE transport in openAgentEventStream

The stream sat on hey-api's createSseClient, which is built as a simple
self-retrying consumer: it throws a bare Error on non-2xx, swallows failures
by completing the generator, yields data without the SSE event or id, keeps
Last-Event-ID sticky across attempts, and runs its own retry loop. A resilient
client needs the opposite of each, so the file inverted all five through a
fetch wrapper, an onSseError capture, sseMaxRetryAttempts: 1, an onSseEvent
watchdog, and a manually driven iterator, with the state for each spread
across closures. Upstream has not changed (hey-api/hey-api#2908, #3018,
#4321), and even with those fixes the retry loop would still need disabling.

Replace only that helper. The generator is still used for URL building,
header merging, request interceptors, types, and zod.

- server-sent-events.ts: a pure incremental text/event-stream parser that
  yields message data; CR/CRLF handled without the split-chunk bug.
- openConnection(): one physical connection with the Response in hand, a
  read deadline that aborts a per-attempt controller, AbortSignal.any over
  the caller's signal, and every outcome thrown as a classified error.
- openAgentEventStream(): the session: cursor, replay filter, backoff, and
  connection-state callbacks. Public signature and return type unchanged.
- Frames are discriminated with the generated zod schemas; the durable
  cursor keeps accepting unknown event kinds.
- validate-response.ts: schemaMismatch() shared with the generated
  validators.

AgentEventStreamError gains retryAfterMs. Existing tests are untouched;
parser unit tests and a request header/credentials parity test are added.

* Return 424 upstream_unavailable for transient MCP upstream failures

Transient failures from a user-configured MCP server or its authorization
server (5xx, 429, timeouts, connection errors) now return 424 with code
upstream_unavailable so callers can retry, while definitive rejections keep
returning 422. Applies to OAuth discovery, dynamic client registration, and
tool discovery including the auth probe.

storage and encoding faults, ErrCredential for auth secrets that cannot be
used or refreshed, and ErrRefreshBusy for lease contention. Tool discovery
maps these to 500, 422 or 424, and 409 respectively instead of reporting
every failure as an unreachable server.

Two review findings, both about recording a machine as ready when it is not.

waitForDaemon returned success for any non-terminal run once the settle window
elapsed. The API contract defines `pending` as "accepted but has not started
yet because an earlier run on the same session is still in flight", so a queued
run was being read as a started daemon. It now requires `running`, and gives up
with the state it saw rather than waiting forever — the boot script installs
omnarad before exec'ing it, which outlasts the settle window, so the timeout is
separate from it and shortened in tests the same way.

refuses to build a client with no placement, so an empty value produced a
machine record that could never be woken. Rejecting it at the write site keeps
the invariant where the information exists; unikraft refuses the same way at
its wake.

Verified it fails without the fix.

* fix(arker): stop adopting an in-flight daemon

startDaemon listed the VM's runs, and if an omnarad boot was already in flight
it adopted that run and skipped writing the boot script. No other provider
inspects the guest this way — they adopt the machine on a retry and then do
their provisioning step.

Adopting modelled omnara's daemon lifecycle inside the provider, and got it
wrong: a later provision mints a fresh daemon token, so skipping the write left
the guest running the previous attempt's credentials and machine env while the
pool recorded the machine as provisioned.

startDaemon is now write the script, run it, wait for `running`. Each attempt
delivers its own token and env. What happens to a daemon a previous attempt
left running is omnara's to decide: it already revokes sibling tokens when a
runtime registers.

Replaces the three adoption tests with one that pins the simpler contract —
every provision writes the boot script and starts the daemon. Verified it fails
when the write is skipped.

alongside unikraft and modal, which are the other two that declare

* fix(arker): bound the daemon wait by the context, not just a fixed ceiling

`defaultDaemonStartTimeout` exists so a stuck boot reports the run state
rather than a bare cancellation, but it is measured from the first poll
while the manager's deadline has been running since Fork. Everything
before that poll -- the fork, writing the boot script, and now cancelling
a stale daemon -- spends the same minute, so five seconds of headroom was
not reliably enough and the outer deadline could still fire first.

waitForDaemon now takes the smaller of that ceiling and what the context
actually has left, reserving a short margin so it ends, and reports, just
before the manager gives up on it.

The timeout message reports elapsed time instead of the ceiling. Quoting
a budget that was never spent sends whoever reads the error looking for
the wrong thing.

* fix(arker): recover a lost vm id when observing runtime state

ObserveRuntimeState returned `unknown` as soon as the target had no
provider resource id, so it never reached the allocation-name lookup that
InspectMachine supports. A VM whose id was never persisted -- a fork
response that did not come back, a failed resource write -- stayed live,
billable, and invisible to reconciliation, which could neither recover
nor terminate it.

I had declined this on the grounds that a machine mid-provision has no id
yet and would be reported terminated. That is wrong. Both candidate
queries inner-join `daemon_runtime_connection_facts` on the machine's
`current_daemon_runtime_id`, so a machine only becomes an observation
target once its omnarad has connected, which it cannot do without a VM. A
machine still being provisioned has no such row and is never observed. An
id missing at this point was LOST, not not-yet-assigned, and the name
lookup is exactly the right recovery.

The test that asserted the old behaviour now asserts the new contract,
including that the observation carries the recovered id -- without that,
cleanup still has nothing to delete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(arker): the context clamp must not shorten the wait below the settle window

Bugbot caught a bug I introduced in c50619fd. Bounding the daemon wait by
the caller's remaining context is right, but the clamp could drag
hardDeadline in FRONT of the settle window -- and success is only
concluded once the daemon has held `running` through that window. With
less than roughly five seconds of context left, a perfectly healthy boot
was therefore reported as stuck, which is the opposite of what bounding
the wait was for. I traded one misleading error for another.

The hard deadline is now never earlier than the settle deadline. If the
context genuinely cannot afford the settle, ctx.Done() ends the wait and
says so, rather than blaming a daemon that was doing nothing wrong.

The regression test was checked against the unfixed code, where it fails
with "is still running after 0s" -- absurd on its face and exactly the
symptom.

* test(arker): cover the settle-window clamp against a real daemon

The unit test for this drives a fake. This drives a real daemon on a real
VM: starts a long-running boot under the command waitForDaemon polls,
confirms Arker reports it `running`, then waits with deliberately less

That leaves one branch in this provider without live coverage, and it is
not reachable: ProvisionMachine's refusal of a VM with an empty
BaseURL(). The SDK will not build a client without either a BaseURL or a
provider+region pair ("Provider and Region are required together unless
BaseURL is supplied"), and a VM's base is always one or the other, so a
successful fork cannot produce an empty endpoint. The guard defends
against a response shape the SDK structurally cannot emit, and stays

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* revert(arker): match every other provider and bail on an empty resource id

8d07a818 made ObserveRuntimeState fall through to InspectMachine's name
lookup when the id was missing. Bugbot pointed out it cannot work:
`runtimeObservationMatches` requires the observation's id to equal the
candidate's, and in this scenario the candidate's id is empty -- that IS
the scenario -- so a successful recovery is guaranteed to be discarded.
The only observation that passes is one that recovered nothing.

I then argued Arker should keep it because the other providers have no
name-based lookup. That was wrong and I had not checked. Every provider
has one: modal's `sandboxByName`, unikraft's `GetInstanceByName`,
daytona's `expectedName`, and blaxel's `InspectMachine` carries the
identical fallback to Arker's. None of their observers uses it. A
provider with the same capability made the opposite choice deliberately,
which is the strongest evidence available that the early return is
correct rather than a limitation.

So this reverts to parity and records WHY in the code, since the reason
is not obvious from the early return alone.

The gap Bugbot originally identified is real and stays open: a VM whose
id was never persisted is live, billable and untracked. Closing it
belongs in the manager -- relaxing that comparison when the candidate's
id is empty -- where it would fix all five providers at once instead of
one doing something the manager throws away. Raised on the thread.

The live test that asserted recovery goes with it. The other four remain
green against a real deployment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(arker): confirm a cancelled daemon actually left the session

Bugbot pointed out that cancelStaleDaemons calls CancelRun and returns
without waiting for the run to leave session 1, which takes one run at a
time. startDaemon then writes the boot script and starts another run
immediately, so if the cancelled one still holds the session the new
daemon sits `pending` and waitForDaemon fails a VM that is otherwise
fine.

It does not reproduce on the provider's own path -- a live retry runs
rather than queueing -- but the failure mode is reachable, and a probe
showed how: CancelRun can answer 404 while the run is still going. That
404 was being treated as success, because its usual meaning is that the
run is already gone. Nothing then distinguishes "already finished" from
"not cancelled at all", and the next run queues behind it.

cancelStaleDaemons now confirms each run reaches a terminal state before
returning, and fails with a message naming the state rather than letting
startDaemon queue behind a run we have already given up on.

The live cancel test also asserted too little: it discarded the retry's
error, so it could not have caught this. It now fails if the retry
reports the daemon still pending.

One note for the next person: `terminalRunStates` holds the API's own
spelling, `cancelled` with two Ls, and carries a nolint for exactly that
reason. It is a wire value, not prose -- a blanket spelling fix across
this file silently breaks terminal-state detection.

make verify-static and go test ./... pass; all four live tests green.

bring its own boxd account and run agent machines on boxd microVMs.

Provider (internal/machinepool/providers/boxd):
- gRPC client against the boxd API with a shared, single-flight session
  token cache (API key -> short-lived JWT), shared connections, and
  transient/rejected/capacity error classification.
- Idempotent provisioning keyed by the deterministic allocation name:
  adopt an existing VM, destroy and recreate a dead one (ErrResourceReplaced),
  and refuse to create more than one live VM per Omnara machine.
- Provider options: snapshot, startup_script, sleep_after_ms, and
  auto_suspend_secs. The daemon parks after sleep_after_ms and boxd suspends
  the VM after auto_suspend_secs of silence; the provider always sends an
  explicit auto-suspend window because snapshot restores otherwise inherit
  the source VM's window.
- Wake path: WakeMachine execs a local poke against the daemon's wake
  listener, which makes the boxd proxy resume a suspended VM before the
  next turn. Measured 0.6-1.2s from suspended to daemon back online.
- Boot payload delivered over Exec (boxd does not apply CreateVm env), with
  an idempotent launcher that unlinks the payload once the daemon is up.
- Size classes validated against boxd's 1x4G / 2x8G / 4x16G offerings, with
  snapshot-versus-size conflict detection in PrepareProvisioning.
- Runtime observer over ListVms for runtime protection.
- Live smoke and wake tests gated on OMNARA_BOXD_TEST_* env vars.

Machine pool manager:
- New providers.ErrResourceNotCreated and providers.WithRetryDelay. A
  provider that observed a synchronous refusal (capacity, invalid request)
  wraps ErrResourceNotCreated so the manager stops retrying at once and
  cleanup finalizes the row immediately instead of holding it in
  delete_failed for the 24h missing-resource grace period. Capacity refusals
  also carry a 10 minute retry hint and surface boxd's message on the
  Machines page.

Surfaces:
- OpenAPI boxd branch, regenerated Go and TypeScript SDK types.
- Web: boxd in the pool dialog, resource fields, grant overrides, and agent
  config extraction. MachinePoolDialogState split into per-provider helpers.
- Docs for pools, overview, and self-hosting configuration.
- CI/Makefile: boxd live tests join the sandbox provider live suite;
  generated boxdv1 code excluded from golangci-lint.

* fix(boxd): pick size classes in the pool form and keep reason text valid

Addresses the three review findings on the boxd provider.

Pool dialog: boxd only offers fixed machine shapes, but the form accepted
any positive CPU and memory numbers, defaulted to 1 vCPU / 1 GB, and kept
1 GB when switching from Blaxel, so Create was enabled and the API refused
the pool. The form now shows a size picker for providers that declare size
classes (1x4 GB, 2x8 GB, 4x16 GB) and a "Snapshot or org default" choice
that leaves the size to boxd, which the API and docs already allowed. While
the size is left to the provider the per-machine limits are required and
stand in for it in validation and in the derived totals; an edit that
switches to it clears the stored defaults with explicit nulls. The pool
form helpers moved to their own module to stay under the line cap.

Lifecycle reason text: bootstrap and wake stderr was cut on a byte count and
forwarded unchanged, so a NUL, invalid UTF-8, or a multi-byte character on
the cut turned the failure record itself into a Postgres write error. The
tail is now made valid UTF-8, NUL is replaced, and the cut lands on a
character boundary.

Create classification: AlreadyExists no longer counts as proof that no
resource exists. A held name means the holder is usually this machine from
an earlier attempt, which the next attempt adopts through the lookup that
precedes every create; if the lookup keeps missing it, cleanup keeps the
missing-resource grace period instead of finalizing on a code that asserts
a resource is there.

Verified end to end on a local stack against a real boxd org: pools
created from the form's exact payloads (2x8 GB and size left to boxd), the
old 1 vCPU / 1 GB default now rejected by the API, agents on both pools
running commands on 2 vCPU / 8 GB and 4 vCPU / 16 GB machines, edit
round-trips in both directions, and the dashboard dialog itself creating,
editing, and deleting a boxd pool.

feat: expose observability as a public Go module (#611)

* feat: expose observability as a public Go module

Move the generic wide-event logging (internal/log) and the Prometheus
recorders (internal/metrics) into a nested module,
github.com/omnara-ai/omnara/observability, so other services can import a
pinned version instead of forking it. Service-specific event helpers
(internal/log/logent) stay in the control plane. Call sites import
observability/wideevent under their existing name (log or logpkg), so only
import lines change.

The module also merges improvements from the hosted SaaS fork:
- Event.Escalate raises a level past an earlier pin; HTTP 5xx now escalates.
- Start helper, exported OnlyCanceled, and ResponseRecorder.Abort.
- Bounded trace buffers keep failure-first selection without retaining
  every record until Done; Done skips flushing when the level is disabled.
- Provider credential shapes are scrubbed from log strings.
- metrics.WithNamespace, HTTPRecorder.Start, and JobRecorder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(observability): share request completion and keep escalation upward

- Add observability/httprequest, which emits each request's wide event and
  metrics observation from one final status and recovers handler panics.
  The control plane now uses it instead of the promhttp middleware, so a
  panic after a partial response records the abort in both the log and
  the request count and duration. HTTPRecorder.Middleware and
  SetHTTPRequestStatusCode are removed.
- Escalate sets a minimum level instead of replacing the computed one, so
  it never lowers an event that would otherwise log at error.
- Run observability tests under race-unit and format every module with
  make fmt using the fmt-check file set.
- Drop comments that restate the code.

The rebase formatted these files with an older gofmt, which CI's

* test(httpapi): close the daemon socket only after Accept hijacks it

TestDaemonSocketExitAppearsInRequestLog closed the client as soon as the
handshake response arrived. If that close landed before Accept finished
hijacking the connection, net/http's pending background read canceled
the request context first, so the recorded cancel source was unknown
instead of the socket's own cause. The race shows up on main too under
load. Wait for Accept before closing.

fix(httpapi): marshal JSON responses with json.Marshal to resolve reflected-XSS alert (#630)

CodeQL go/reflected-xss (alert #36) traced user input from OAuth authorize,
integration callbacks and OpenAPI request decoding into the wideevent
ResponseRecorder.Write sink. The responses were JSON with an explicit
application/json Content-Type, but CodeQL loses that through the recorder
wrapper and does not treat json.Encoder as a sanitizer. json.Marshal is a
recognized sanitizer and HTML-escapes identically, so switch httpjson.Write,
apierror's ResponseError.write and the Discord interaction responder to it,
appending the newline Encoder.Encode wrote so bodies stay byte-identical.

perf: scale agent execution with typed execution state and a claim dispatcher (#631)

* perf: scale agent execution with typed execution state, a claim dispatcher, and owned continuation

Replace history-derived scheduling with an agent execution engine. Each agent
has a typed execution head of pointers, monotonic boundaries and summaries
recomputed at commit, plus immutable opening lineage on model contexts, config
changes and checkpoints. One pure selector decides next work for claim, owned
continuation, release and recovery. Semantic transitions run through a
cell-bound unit of work that plans locks up front in sorted order, supports
savepoints, and publishes each changed agent's head and queue in two pipelined
statements before enqueueing webhooks and post-commit notifications. Execution
writes live in a private query package enforced by SQL rules and a Go analyzer.

Workers run a bounded claim dispatcher, keep an owned agent across ready steps
within a configurable budget, and accept model output, select and prepare the
next call in one transaction.

Migration 052 builds every existing agent's execution state from history,
validates it, and drops the history frontier functions. It requires a
writer-stop maintenance window.

Also fixes:
- continuations stranded when a turn carried unanswered inputs from an earlier
  turn
- child-before-parent and machine/parent lock-order hazards
- subagent launch reusing a machine grant deleted while it waited
- project and organization deletion skipping event webhooks

and invalidating it otherwise, so publication reloads only when a selection is
stale. Move webhook eligibility capture into publication, simplify the facts

  together. The check runs under the agent lock after the idempotency

- Accept a child's results, failures and questions to its parent past the
  cap; they still count toward it.
- Leave integration inbox deliveries pending for retry, record a skipped

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: commit input attachments with the accepted input

  rows inside the admission transaction, after the idempotency and
  capacity checks. A rejected submission leaves no artifact rows.
- Delete prepared blobs after a definite rejection or an idempotent
  replay, and keep them when the commit outcome is unknown.
- Match idempotent replays by attachment content type, filename, digest

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make input and config-change idempotency key-only

A retry with a known idempotency key returns the stored input or config
change without comparing the request. This removes the field and content
comparisons, the attachment replay matching and the actor lookup they
needed, so a retry after promoting a queued input to steering returns the
original instead of conflicting. A config-change replay now returns the
stored config, input and event before preparing a new config.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: lock the parent up front for predictable parent effects

Roots whose transition will report to the parent now plan the agent family
before writing: a model output that ends the turn without tool calls, a
terminal model failure and a terminal compaction failure. These complete
in one attempt instead of rolling back to add the parent. Outputs that
call tools still lock only the child. AcceptOutput and the planning use
one shared rule for which outputs report to the parent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: tighten execution engine hygiene

Lock the root and parent before inserting a nested subagent, treat a null
terminal process observation as absent, and authorize config-change replays
against the current caller.

Move reconstruction, repair, and other test-only engine entry points into
integration-tagged support, delete the duplicate child commands and fake-only
executor fallbacks, and make integration Once helpers re-plan lock sets without
retrying SQLSTATE failures.

Look up each idempotency key once per request, insert prepared artifacts in one
place, source the pending-input cap and retry/lease policy from single
constants, and drop dead exported identifiers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: key worker replays on identity and consolidate execution helpers

Worker replays of outputs, failures, compaction, tool results, and question
openings return the stored result for the same identity and terminal state
instead of comparing payloads; lease fencing and terminal-kind conflicts are
unchanged. Human interaction resolution keeps its documented contract.

Replace Unit.LockAgent with store helpers that return handles, share the
interaction-cancel, model-failure, tool-completion, and process-settlement
paths, drop the circular final check from migration 052, and route plain
transactions through storeutil.RetryTransaction.

Replace self-referential history tests and wall-clock ratios with a stored
head versus reconstruction oracle and deterministic bounds, share integration
plan and tracing helpers, and restore merge-base wrapping on untouched code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep identity checks on worker replays and custom tool results

Model failure replays match the recorded recovery kind, so a retry, terminal
failure, or compaction cannot replay as another. Output replays reject tool
call IDs that differ from the stored proposals. Custom tool results are
accepted only while the call is ready, matching the documented first-result
contract.

Route the remaining inline process settlements through the shared helpers,
drop the checkpoint summary comparison, and check the stored head mid-turn in
the reconstruction oracle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: recheck config idempotency after the config change lock

A duplicate config change that found no stored key before waiting on the
agent machine-source lock now looks again after acquiring it, so it replays
the original result instead of failing the current-config guard after a
later edit. The early lookup still lets committed replays skip integration
gates.

The reconstruction oracle compares persisted head columns, the creation
linearity test bounds tuples read per agent including trigger work, and a
backlog-full inbox failure keeps the partial-delivery notice when some
recipients already received the message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: sample execution heads for drift and share profile locks on launch

Maintenance samples up to ten active agents every five minutes in read-only
snapshots, rebuilds each head from current-turn history through indexed
lookups, and reports mismatches through the maintenance job metrics and a
structured log. Full-history lineage validation stays in the test oracle.

Launch, inbox launch preflight, and cron profile checks take a key-share lock
on the agent profile, so concurrent launches from one profile no longer
serialize; retarget and delete keep their exclusive lock. Route discovery and
the redundant launch-key lookup move out of the quota-held section.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: check creation quotas at commit and stop scanning orgs for authorization

Agent, config, machine and daemon-token creation quotas are checked once at
the commit boundary: deferred constraints are drained, the quota keys are
locked in a fixed order as the final locks, limits are resolved once per org,
and the counts are read before COMMIT. Limits stay exact and quota errors keep
their original message. Launch reads the parent's machine sources under a
shared gate, which config changes and other writers still exclude.

The authorization roles view marks its active-projects CTE NOT MATERIALIZED,
so principal filters reach the organization and project indexes instead of
scanning both tables. The drift sampler loads current-turn outputs in one
query and bounds each snapshot with a transaction timeout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf: plan daemon process offers in milliseconds instead of tens

ListDaemonProcessOffers joined about a dozen relations through views, so
each custom plan cost tens of milliseconds while execution took a fraction
of one, and that planning was repaid whenever cached plans were invalidated.
It now reads processes alone, checks runtime authority and binding
eligibility with EXISTS, and looks up the originating config's git
credentials in a shell-only scalar subquery. Results are unchanged.

A profile retargeted between the unlocked read and the launch lock now
retries the launch with the new config instead of returning a conflict.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

The drift sampler walks active agents in primary-key order from an
in-memory cursor and wraps, so archived agents no longer crowd out the
sample. An active agent without an execution head reports head_missing, and
readiness timestamps are only normalized when both values are present.
Item counters start at zero so the documented windowed alert clears after a
repair.

A launch whose profile keeps changing until its retries run out returns a
conflict instead of an internal error.

No path has ever set an agent input to rejected: inserts are always
received, and admission resolves or cancels. Inputs that fail validation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: remove owned worker continuation

Each claim now runs one model step or tool batch and releases the lease;
a still-ready agent returns to the ready queue like on main. Removes the
keep-going loop and its two settings, the kernel's fused
accept-and-prepare-next path, AcceptModelOutputAndAdvance,

* fix: defer an agent whose claim keeps failing

A claim that fails after selecting an agent rolls back, so the same agent
stayed first in the ready queue and every claim loop retried it. The
failed agent's wakeup now moves one minute out in a short follow-up
transaction, the worker logs the agent and counts
omnara_worker_claim_deferrals_total, and claiming continues immediately.

fix: stop claiming after cancellation and harden live provider tests (#652)

* fix: stop the claim loop from claiming after cancellation

When the claim loop reached its slot select after cancellation, both the
cancelled context and a just-freed slot could be ready, and Go picks one
at random. Half the time the loop claimed again during shutdown. Real
claims fail on the cancelled context, but the worker test's fake store
does not, and its third release blocked forever, which made
TestWorkerLoopContinuesAfterTurnFailure hang under CI load.

The loop now returns the slot and exits if the context was cancelled
while it waited.

#446 made the compaction runner treat a max_tokens summary of the
smallest source as summary_truncated and schedule a retry instead of
publishing it, as TestRunnerNeverPublishesSmallestTruncatedSummary
specifies. The live provider test still expected the truncated summary
to become a checkpoint, so Live Provider Tests failed on main from #446
onward. The truncated case now asserts the retry path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: harden live provider checks for compaction recovery

A truncated compaction summary can contain no text, so only completed
summaries must have text; truncated ones must record the provider's
usage. The live compaction recall test accepts more than one compaction
round, keeping its bridge-answer and idle checks. Live provider steps no
longer skip later providers after one fails; each runs unless the run
is cancelled or setup failed, and the job still fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: fail the live recall test on runaway compaction

Allowing more than one compaction round removed the exact counts that
used to rule out compaction looping. The test now fails immediately,
with the counts, once checkpoints or budget failures exceed three
rounds, instead of passing when an answer eventually appears.

docs(api): describe the parameters and operations behind Omnara's MCP tools (#670)

Glama graded Omnara's MCP tool definitions C (2.5). The two weakest
dimensions were parameter semantics and usage guidelines:

- Path ID parameters had no descriptions anywhere (orgID was undescribed
  in all 71 tools that take it), so only 44% of tool parameters were
  described. Every path ID parameter now names what it is and its
  prefix, and most request-body fields on the create/update operations
  are described. Every tool with parameters is now above 80% coverage.
- 44 operations had no description or only an ordering note, so their
  tools showed just the summary or that note. Each now says what the
  operation does and, where relevant, its side effects, conditions, and
  what it returns, and covers only that operation. List operations still
  state their default order.

Also corrects Update project model grant, which said agents use the
configured-model revision pinned at launch. Each model call reads the
model's current revision (ExecutionModelRevision in createAttempt).

Approves one oasdiff finding on Create agent: oasdiff identifies inline
anyOf subschemas by content, so the new descriptions on AgentConfigID
and CreateAgentConfigRequest.source_format read as removed subschemas.
The request schema is unchanged.

fix: read the model transcript after the prepare transaction commits (#672)

* fix: read the model transcript after the prepare transaction commits

The prepare transaction holds the agent row lock. Since #631 it also read
the whole transcript, so agents with long histories held the lock for
seconds and blocked daemon reports and other writers to the same agent.
Commit the prepare first and let the context builder read the transcript
through the store, as resume steps and pre-#631 main do.

Also match the drift alert on outcome only. Prometheus renames the
metric's own job label to exported_job, so the documented matcher never
fired.

fix: stop NUL bytes in process output from hanging tool calls (#674)

* fix: stop process output NUL bytes from wedging daemon reads

Process output containing raw NUL bytes made the server reject daemon
reports with a transient storage_unavailable error, so read_process
reconnect-looped forever and frozen process reports retried forever.

- daemon: replace NUL with a one-byte "?" (matching the existing
  invalid UTF-8 handling) wherever output bytes become report text, so
  byte cursors and the server's output-within-span check still hold
- server: dbsafe errors now wrap dbsafe.ErrInvalidText and daemon
  reports that fail it are permanently rejected as validation_failed
- daemon: a rejected read observation fails just that read with
  invalid_read_observation instead of tearing down the websocket
- daemon: log the cause when the connection is lost

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: show process output NUL bytes as U+2400

Replace NUL with "␀" (U+2400) instead of "?", and measure process
output in raw bytes, counting each "␀" as one byte, wherever it is
checked against its cursor span, max_bytes, or the frozen-output cap.
Invalid UTF-8 still becomes "?".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: show invalid UTF-8 in process output as U+FFFD

Replace invalid UTF-8 in process output with U+FFFD instead of "?",
and count each U+FFFD as one raw byte in OutputRawBytes. A run of
invalid bytes collapses into one U+FFFD, so the count is a lower bound,
which only loosens the upper-bound span and size checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: retry storage-unavailable read reports and fail NUL reads on the server

Retry a read report the server rejects as storage_unavailable with backoff
before failing the read as storage_unavailable, instead of failing it as an
invalid observation. Reject NUL output in server read validation so the
server records the failed read itself. Rename the output length helper to
MinOutputRawBytes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: Improve agent edit UI (#348)

* ui improvements

* Improve agent edit UI for profiles and agents

* fix ci

* convert machines to machine binding id

* review fixes, adapt to document based yaml

* Refresh agent on config save conflict so discard loads the latest config

A 409 left the cached agent (and its current_config_id) stale, so
discarding remounted the editor with the same old source and expected id,
conflicting again on retry. Invalidate the agent query on 409 (awaited
before the mutation settles) and make discard re-snapshot from the live
query instead of falling back to the stale snapshot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Skip already-listed machines when granting from a source row

Granting from a row's combobox could duplicate machine_name entries and
reassign a selected row while keeping its cwd/env overlays. Drop names
already in the list, fill the current row only when it's empty, and
append the rest as fresh rows. Also apply prettier formatting CI flagged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Reconcile agent config editor with main's React Doctor refactor

The rebase onto main replayed this branch's editor rewrite over the
React Doctor restructuring (#308), so re-apply main's changes the replay
dropped and bring the editor suite in line with the new CI gate:

- Restore main's machines.ts (atomic connectByoMachine) and DataTable
  column API in AgentProfilesSection, re-applying this branch's edits.
- Adapt the machine source comboboxes to the new resource-combobox
  value contract via lightweight option objects.
- Fix React Doctor findings: refs instead of render state for
  handler-only values, drop compiler-redundant memoization, set-based
  lookups, and resolve the skills cache during render instead of an
  effect. Ignore the parent-callback rules for the editor files, whose
  children intentionally report yaml/dirty/availability upward.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Parse the config source once per editor via a serialization session

deserializeBasicConfig and applyBasicConfig each took the raw source, so
every builder change re-parsed the baseline and re-extracted it into a
second draft. createBasicConfigSession(source) parses and extracts once
for the editor's lifetime and returns { initialDraft, apply }; apply
clones the pristine document per call so reverting a field restores the
entry's original formatting. The form takes the session instead of
initialConfig + baselineSource.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Replace hand-rolled config extraction with a zod schema

extractBasicConfig walked the parsed document with manual typeof checks,
per-entry key allowlists, and generic list/map plumbing. A zod schema
now declares the builder-representable subset directly: strictObject is
the key allowlist, looseObject is the tolerated-extras top level, and
what remains is the typed mapping into draft rows. On the apply side,
tools and MCP entries compare by wire form, removing the parallel
comparable shapes; only machine sources keep a distinct comparison form,
since pool-resolution backfill changes their wire output.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Consolidate the config editors and slim the mode machine

The agent panel editor and profile editor duplicated the mode machine
wiring, blocked/dirty/saveBlocked derivation, and the tabs/builder/YAML
layout. useAgentConfigEditor now owns that state and
AgentConfigEditorFields the shared markup; the editors keep only their
form, messages, and footer.

The mode reducer tracks just the hand-edited YAML (null while mirroring
the builder) instead of holding both buffers; builder YAML lives with
the component that produces it. wireConfig is gone — the no-document
fallback applies onto an empty Document through the same path as every
other serialization. The form's duplicate BasicConfigDraft type is
replaced by BasicConfig.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Strip comments and give the builder form a document-facing hook

Remove the explanatory comments this PR added across the frontend and
Go changes, keeping only functional directives. useAgentBuilderForm now
owns the builder draft: it seeds from the session's document, exposes
form values and named setters, and reports serialized YAML plus the
blocked flag; AgentConfigBasicForm is rendering only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fold agentConfigBasic into useAgentBuilderForm

The draft types, empty draft, and completeness check belong to the form.
isBasicConfigComplete becomes per-section validators (draftValid,
machineSourceValid, mcpServerValid, mcpServerNamesUnique) private to the
hook; other modules import the draft types from useAgentBuilderForm.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move the document session and apply into useAgentBuilderForm

The hook is the only thing that applies drafts to the document, so
agentConfigBasicYaml.ts folds into it: session creation, the
diff-and-rewrite apply, and the wire serializers now live with the form
that uses them. The two test files and their fixtures merge into
useAgentBuilderForm.test.ts. agentConfigBasicExtract.ts stays separate
as the schema-validated read side (folding it in would break the
500-line lint limit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Adopt builder-representable YAML edits when switching back to the builder

Switching from the YAML tab to the builder previously always demanded
discarding hand edits. Now the typed YAML runs through
createBasicConfigSession: when it is builder-representable it becomes
the new session baseline and the form reseeds from it, so the edits
carry over; the confirm-and-discard dialog remains only for YAML the
builder cannot represent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Derive builder YAML from the form instead of mirroring it upward

The editor held builderYaml state fed by an onYamlChange callback
because the draft lived inside the form component. useAgentBuilderForm
no longer takes a callback: the editor hook owns the form, and yaml and
blocked are derived from the draft (session.apply(draft)). That deletes
the mirror state, the callback effect, and the formGeneration remount on
YAML adoption, which now just resets the draft. AgentConfigBasicForm
takes the form object and stays render-only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix YAML adoption: collapse the fork with an explicit action

Adopting builder-representable YAML edits never worked: switchMode
collapsed the fork by dispatching editor-yaml-changed with the forked
text itself, which the reducer's no-op guard swallowed, so switch-mode
still saw a fork and raised the discard dialog for every edit. A
dedicated adopt-yaml-edits action enters the builder and clears the
fork; reducer tests pin the transitions. The dialog copy now says it
only appears for YAML the builder can't represent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Prune library-behavior and duplicate tests

Drop the form tests that only exercised the yaml/zod libraries
(formatting-variant parsing, explicit empty parameters, irregular
instruction indentation) and merge the discard reducer test into the
confirm-dialog transition it belongs to; adopt keeps its own regression
test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* gofmt agent_config_changes_store.go

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Regenerate sqlc code after SQL comment removal

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Integrate main's agent templates with the builder-form create page

Rebase reconciliation: main added an onboarding template flow built on
agentConfigBasicSerialization, which this branch had replaced with the
useAgentBuilderForm session API. Rewrite CreateAgentFormView on the new
API (template menu, ?template= prefill, message placeholder preserved),
re-point agentTemplates at the builder module, and delete the retired
serialization module. Carry main's GB memory rename through the builder
form, extract, and machine sources field. Regenerate the TS SDK from the
merged spec.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Serialize an untouched builder form to an empty YAML document

With no baseline config, applyToDocument wrote empty-string scalars into
a fresh document, so the YAML tab on the create page opened with an
instruction/model skeleton instead of an empty editor and typed YAML
merged into it invalidly. Compare scalars against an empty baseline so
only filled fields are written.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): canonicalize email identity keys (#466)

Email identity keys were lower(trim(email)), so the composed, decomposed
and Punycode spellings of an internationalized domain were three
different identities: logins and invitations missed each other and a
second account could be verified for the same mailbox.

Derive the key in one place (internal/emailaddr): the domain becomes its
lowercase A-label via UTS #46 non-transitional processing with hostname
length rules, the comparison form RFC 9598 §5.5 prescribes; the local
part is lowercased and otherwise left alone, since RFC 9598 §5.7 forbids
transforming it and merging two spellings a mail server might treat as
different mailboxes would attach an OIDC login to the wrong account.
CreateUserEmail derives the key itself instead of trusting callers.
Lookups stay single-key and no queries change. Every pure-ASCII key is a
fixed point of the new rule (property-tested), so existing rows keep
their keys and no data migration is needed.

emailaddr.Equal replaces the EqualFold comparison of OIDC id-token and
userinfo emails. The password policy receives the address rather than
the key and rejects a password containing either spelling.

Supersedes #409.

fix: make agent event streams resilient (#421)

* fix: make agent event streams resilient

* chore: prune redundant comments

* fix(api): reconcile missed SSE event wakeups

* docs: focus SSE guide on client behavior

* refactor(sdk): own the SSE transport in openAgentEventStream

The stream sat on hey-api's createSseClient, which is built as a simple
self-retrying consumer: it throws a bare Error on non-2xx, swallows failures
by completing the generator, yields data without the SSE event or id, keeps
Last-Event-ID sticky across attempts, and runs its own retry loop. A resilient
client needs the opposite of each, so the file inverted all five through a
fetch wrapper, an onSseError capture, sseMaxRetryAttempts: 1, an onSseEvent
watchdog, and a manually driven iterator, with the state for each spread
across closures. Upstream has not changed (hey-api/hey-api#2908, #3018,
#4321), and even with those fixes the retry loop would still need disabling.

Replace only that helper. The generator is still used for URL building,
header merging, request interceptors, types, and zod.

- server-sent-events.ts: a pure incremental text/event-stream parser that
  yields message data; CR/CRLF handled without the split-chunk bug.
- openConnection(): one physical connection with the Response in hand, a
  read deadline that aborts a per-attempt controller, AbortSignal.any over
  the caller's signal, and every outcome thrown as a classified error.
- openAgentEventStream(): the session: cursor, replay filter, backoff, and
  connection-state callbacks. Public signature and return type unchanged.
- Frames are discriminated with the generated zod schemas; the durable
  cursor keeps accepting unknown event kinds.
- validate-response.ts: schemaMismatch() shared with the generated
  validators.

AgentEventStreamError gains retryAfterMs. Existing tests are untouched;
parser unit tests and a request header/credentials parity test are added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(sdk): harden the event stream connection and reuse client.request

- A connection attempt shares the 35s stall deadline with reads, so a hung
  fetch surfaces as a reconnect instead of silence.
- Retry-After can lengthen the computed backoff but never shorten it; a
  persistent 503 with Retry-After: 0 no longer hot-loops.
- Durable frames are classified before error envelopes, matching the open
  event_kind cursor rule.
- The request half goes through client.request({ parseAs: 'stream' }) so
  auth and response interceptors and client config apply to the stream like
  every other call. A per-attempt AbortController replaces AbortSignal.any,
  which browsers before 2024 lack.
- The SSE parser keeps an in-progress message as chunks so a large frame is

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Return 424 upstream_unavailable for transient MCP upstream failures

Transient failures from a user-configured MCP server or its authorization
server (5xx, 429, timeouts, connection errors) now return 424 with code
upstream_unavailable so callers can retry, while definitive rejections keep
returning 422. Applies to OAuth discovery, dynamic client registration, and
tool discovery including the auth probe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Distinguish internal, credential, and busy failures in MCP tool discovery

The MCP manager now tags errors at their origin: ErrInternal for Omnara
storage and encoding faults, ErrCredential for auth secrets that cannot be
used or refreshed, and ErrRefreshBusy for lease contention. Tool discovery
maps these to 500, 422 or 424, and 409 respectively instead of reporting
every failure as an unreachable server.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
